mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% over the last three months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 60-day forward returns in improving labor market periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over the last quarter indicates strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns during periods of GDP growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% over the last two months signals increased supply-side activity, which boosts economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of increased industrial production are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 5% over the last two months signals a weakening in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of reduced economic demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 60-day forward returns in periods of decreased housing starts are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds the inflation rate (CPIAUCSL annualized), it signals a real tightening of monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of real monetary tightening are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k in 1 month AND UNRATE decrease > 0.2%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 5-day forward returns in periods of strong labor market signals are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last quarter indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns during periods of increased consumer spending are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
